nodes.rationale: Chosen for ~2KB size, an immutable sandbox API (every mutation returns a new instance, preventing long debugging sessions) and opt-in internationalization that stays out of the build unless used.

nodes.label: Cross-domain Strategy: Vite Forward Proxy / Nginx Reverse Proxy

nodes.label: sa CLI (packages/scripts)
nodes.rationale: Built-in command line tool provided by packages/scripts offering cleanup, update-pkg, git-commit, git-commit-verify, changelog, release and gen-route commands.

nodes.label: Conventional Commits Standard
nodes.rationale: Commit message standard enforced project-wide: sa git-commit generates compliant messages and sa git-commit-verify validates them; PRs must use pnpm commit.

nodes.label: simple-git-hooks (3)
nodes.rationale: Pre-commit hook runner enforcing type/lint checks; docs argue runtime-driven JS debugging breeds unmaintainable code while SoybeanAdmin's 100% TypeScript type coverage makes hooks worth keeping. Can be skipped per-commit with --no-verify or removed from package.json (not recommended).

nodes.label: useTable
nodes.rationale: Deliberately UI-agnostic: only manages request, data transformation, column configuration and column visibility (checks), so any UI library can wrap it. columns() is a factory so reloadColumns can rebuild titles (e.g. after locale change) without losing checked state.

nodes.label: useNaiveTable
nodes.rationale: Naive UI adapter over useTable: supplies getColumnChecks/getColumns internally, generates stable internal keys for selection/expand columns so they participate in visibility control, computes scrollX = sum(width||minWidth||120), and watches appStore.locale to reloadColumns automatically on i18n change.

nodes.label: useNaivePaginatedTable
nodes.rationale: Adds pagination (PaginationProps), mobilePagination for small screens, and getDataByPage; onPaginationParamsChange must sync page/pageSize back to search params; call getDataByPage(1) when filter conditions change.

nodes.label: useTableOperate
nodes.rationale: Encapsulates common CRUD UI state for drawer/dialog flows: drawerVisible, operateType, editingData (located by idKey), checkedRowKeys; onDeleted/onBatchDeleted call getData to refresh after successful deletion.

nodes.label: defaultTransform
nodes.rationale: Converts the unified backend pagination structure (records/current/size/total in FlatResponseData) to PaginationData<T>; if the backend response shape differs, a custom transformer with an explicit return type must be supplied instead.

nodes.label: unplugin-icons (2)
nodes.rationale: Converts iconify svg json data into Vue components at build time, so icons are used as components instead of runtime font/img assets.

nodes.label: Local SVG Icon Rendering
nodes.rationale: Local svg files under src/assets/svg-icon are converted into Vue components via unplugin-icons + vite-plugin-svg-icons; prefix is VITE_ICON_LOCAL_PREFIX = {VITE_ICON_PREFIX}-{name}. Because svgs become components once loaded, edits to source svg files are not hot-detected - the project must be restarted to see changes.

nodes.label: SvgIcon Global Component
nodes.rationale: Globally registered component for dynamic icon rendering by name: the icon prop takes an iconify icon name, the local-icon prop takes a local svg filename; supports v-for over icon name arrays.

nodes.label: useSvgIconRender
nodes.rationale: Located at packages/hooks/src/use-svg-icon-render.ts; returns SvgIconVNode for render-function usage, the recommended way to supply icons to NaiveUI props that expect VNodes.

nodes.label: Offline Iconify Icon Loading
nodes.rationale: Uses @iconify/vue addCollection with @iconify/json offline icon collection data so specific icon sets (e.g. Ant Design) render without fetching icon data from the network.

nodes.label: SoybeanAdmin (2)
nodes.rationale: Admin management template built on Vue3, Vite, TypeScript, Pinia and UnoCSS with pnpm monorepo architecture, ApiFox online mock, automated file routing, and both static and dynamic permission routing. The main branch is a simplified core-only version; the example branch carries the complete example menu (the preview site content). NaiveUI, AntDesignVue and ElementPlus variants exist; MIT licensed.

nodes.label: Apifox Cloud Mock
nodes.rationale: The project implements mock requests through Apifox's cloud mock function instead of a local mock server; the shared soybean-admin-mock API documentation lives on apifox.com.

nodes.label: SoybeanJS CLI (sa) npm scripts
nodes.rationale: Built-in command line tooling wired into npm scripts: sa cleanup (delete node_modules/dist/lockfile), sa git-commit (Conventional Commits), sa gen-route (generate routes), sa release, sa update-pkg.

nodes.label: App.Service.Response
nodes.rationale: Default backend payload contract {code: string, msg: string, data: T}; must be modified to match the real backend's return type. Env-file codes are strings, so numeric backend codes need type-aligned comparison.

nodes.label: Request Introduction
nodes.rationale: Multiple request environments (dev/test/pre-prod/prod backend addresses) are configured via env files .env.prod/.env.test with VITE_SERVICE_BASE_URL and VITE_OTHER_SERVICE_BASE_URL.

nodes.label: createRequest
nodes.rationale: Returns a request instance that directly returns (convertible) Axios response data; on success the data is returned unwrapped.

nodes.label: createFlatRequest
nodes.rationale: Wraps response data and error information into a flat object so callers handle a unified {error, data} result shape instead of try/catch.

nodes.label: RequestOption (2)
nodes.rationale: Lifecycle hook contract for request instances: onRequest (e.g. attach token header), isBackendSuccess (compare backend code), onBackendFail (e.g. token expiration handling), transformBackendResponse, onError.

nodes.label: VITE_SERVICE_* Code Configuration
nodes.rationale: Env-driven backend code sets: VITE_SERVICE_SUCCESS_CODE (business success), VITE_SERVICE_LOGOUT_CODES (silent logout), VITE_SERVICE_MODAL_LOGOUT_CODES (logout via popup), VITE_SERVICE_EXPIRED_TOKEN_CODES (trigger token refresh); multiple codes separated by commas.

nodes.label: createServiceConfig
nodes.rationale: Located at @/utils/service.ts; creates the service base path plus the string used to match the proxy.

nodes.label: createViteProxy
nodes.rationale: Builds the Vite dev-server proxy table from the configuration produced by createServiceConfig; enabled/disabled via VITE_HTTP_PROXY in the env file.

nodes.label: getServiceBaseURL
nodes.rationale: Returns baseURL (VITE_SERVICE_BASE_URL) and otherBaseURL (VITE_OTHER_SERVICE_BASE_URL) from import.meta.env, switching to proxy paths when isHttpProxy = import.meta.env.DEV && VITE_HTTP_PROXY === 'Y'.

nodes.label: /proxy-* Matching String Pattern
nodes.rationale: SoybeanAdmin uses matching strings like /proxy-default and /proxy-{key} with a rewrite that strips the prefix. This deliberately separates the matching string from the request path so multiple backend services that all contain the same /api path can be proxied without conflicts.

nodes.label: request Instance
nodes.rationale: Typical instance built with createFlatRequest<App.Service.Response, InstanceState>: onRequest injects Bearer token from localStg; isBackendSuccess compares code against VITE_SERVICE_SUCCESS_CODE; onBackendFail branches on logout codes (silent reset), modal logout codes (error dialog + beforeunload guard), and expired token codes (refresh + retry, guarded by isRefreshingToken state); transformBackendResponse returns response.data.data; onError suppresses messages for modal-logout and expired-token codes.

nodes.label: handleRefreshToken
nodes.rationale: Refreshes the expired token and returns a retryable request config; the refreshToken endpoint must not itself return codes in expiredTokenCodes or the flow would loop forever - it should return logout or modal-logout codes instead.

nodes.label: fetchLogin
nodes.rationale: Example API function: POST /auth/accounts/login typed as request<Api.Auth.LoginToken>; with a flat request the result is destructured as {error, data}.

nodes.label: layout.base
nodes.rationale: Layout with common parts: global header, sidebar, footer, etc.

nodes.label: layout.blank
nodes.rationale: Blank layout for single pages.

nodes.label: layout.base$view.[RouteKey] Mixed Component
nodes.rationale: Represents a single-level route: the component string combines layout and view components, split by the dollar sign '$'.

nodes.label: Route Naming Rules
nodes.rationale: Route names are lowercase with hyphens per level; route levels are separated by underscore '_' (demo2_child, demo3_child_child). For manual creation, each level's folder name is the route name and index.vue or [id].vue under it is the route component.

nodes.label: Static Route Mode
nodes.rationale: Route table comes from ./src/router/elegant/routes.ts. meta.constant=true marks routes accessible without login; meta.roles (string[] matched against UserInfo roles) gates permission routes, matched in the pre-route guard phase.

nodes.label: Dynamic Route Mode
nodes.rationale: Route table comes from the fetchGetConstantRoutes and fetchGetUserRoutes interfaces; constant:true returned inside fetchGetUserRoutes does NOT take effect (still requires login) - no-login routes must come from fetchGetConstantRoutes. Preferred pattern is letting the backend filter the route table by role rather than meta.roles. Toggled via VITE_AUTH_ROUTE_MODE (static | dynamic) in .env; the returned route table type must stay consistent with the frontend static route table type.

nodes.label: Elegant Router (2)
nodes.rationale: Plugin the whole routing system is based on: after project start it auto-generates the src/router/elegant directory (route import, definition, conversion files). Routes are byproducts of view files - deleting a file deletes the route; only component and meta survive regeneration. Because <Transition> wraps pages, every page .vue template must have exactly one root element.

nodes.label: RouteKey (3)
nodes.rationale: Union type declaring all route keys for unified route management, auto-generated into src/typings/elegant-router.d.ts from page files under views; RoutePath corresponds one-to-one with RouteKey.

nodes.label: RouteMeta (2)
nodes.rationale: Route meta contract: title, i18nKey (overrides title), roles (access if user has at least one; empty = no permission required), keepAlive, constant (no login, frontend-defined), icon (iconify) / localIcon (src/assets/svg-icon, overrides icon), order, href, hideInMenu, activeMenu (highlight another menu key), multiTab, fixedIndexInTab, query.

nodes.label: useRouterPush
nodes.rationale: Recommended hook encapsulating router.push to make jumping easier; returns routerPush, routerBack, routerPushByKey, toLogin, toggleLoginModule, redirectFromLogin. Must be called with false when used outside setup.

nodes.label: routerPushByKey
nodes.rationale: Pushes by route key (the route's name attribute) with optional query or params.

nodes.label: toLogin
nodes.rationale: Quick jump to the login page; login information must be cleared before jumping, otherwise the route guard intercepts back to the home page.

nodes.label: toggleLoginModule
nodes.rationale: Switches the module mounted on the login page based on LoginModule type: pwd-login | code-login | register | reset-pwd | bind-wechat; removable/extensible as long as the type is kept consistent.

nodes.label: redirectFromLogin
nodes.rationale: After successful login, redirects based on the login page's redirect query parameter; falls back to the home page when no redirect param exists.

nodes.label: File-based Route Structure Conventions
nodes.rationale: views folder layout drives routes: single-level routes use the mixed 'layout.base$view.x' component; secondary routes must not place index.vue beside sibling folders; underscore in folder names splits route levels to keep folder hierarchy shallow (recommended over deep nesting); folders starting with '_' are ignored for aggregation (e.g. _error); [id].vue produces parameter routes with props:true (regex customizable via routePathTransformer); customRoutes only generate route declarations - their route data must be created manually.

nodes.label: Two-level Route Transformation
nodes.rationale: However deep the generated (possibly recursive) route data is, the transformed Vue routes have only two levels: first level is the layout component, second level holds redirect routes or page routes; first-level routes auto-redirect to their first child.

nodes.label: Upstream Sync via cherry-pick
nodes.rationale: Recommended way to take upstream soybean-admin updates into a derived repo: git remote add otherOrigin <soybean-admin url>, git fetch otherOrigin, cherry-pick the wanted commit ids, and resolve conflicts with git cherry-pick --continue.

nodes.label: App.Theme.ThemeSetting
nodes.rationale: Theme setting type declared in src/typings/app.d.ts.

nodes.label: themeSettings (2)
nodes.rationale: Initial theme config in src/theme/settings.ts. In dev the theme config is deliberately not cached so edits show in real time; in prod it is cached in localStorage.

nodes.label: overrideThemeSettings (2)
nodes.rationale: Partial<App.Theme.ThemeSetting> in src/theme/settings.ts; exists because prod caches theme config in localStorage - on each new release the cached config can be overridden through this object.

nodes.label: System Theme Architecture
nodes.rationale: Theme implementation is split into component-library theming and UnoCSS theming; to unify both, a single set of theme configuration variables (theme colors, layout parameters) produces component-library theme variables and theme tokens that derive css variables passed to UnoCSS.

nodes.label: setupLoading
nodes.rationale: In src/plugins/loading.ts; builds the initialization loading animation HTML (system logo svg + 4 pulsing dots spinning + title text) with all element colors dynamically derived from themeColor read from local storage (default #DB5A6B), then replaces #app innerHTML; registered in main.ts setupApp before app.mount('#app').

nodes.label: SystemLogo Component
nodes.rationale: SFC at src/components/common/system-logo.vue rendering <icon-local-logo />; stylable through props, implemented on the local svg icon mechanism.

nodes.label: Storage Cache Wrapper (set/get/remove/clear)
nodes.rationale: Theme data is persisted via localStorage by default; cached data types must be pre-declared in src/typings/storage.d.ts.

nodes.norm_label: auth route modes: static vs dynamic (faq)

nodes.rationale: Route transition animation requires a single root element in the page component; wrap content in one div.

nodes.norm_label: project naming conventions (files kebab-case, components pascalcase)

nodes.label: Why Day.js
nodes.rationale: Chosen for ~2KB size, immutable (sandboxed) instances that prevent mutation bugs, and opt-in i18n that stays out of the build unless used.

nodes.label: CORS and Proxy Solutions
nodes.rationale: Local dev cross-origin is solved by the built-in Vite forward proxy; production cross-origin is solved by Nginx reverse proxy or backend CORS headers.

nodes.label: History Mode 404 on Refresh
nodes.rationale: Nginx serves static files so /login lookup fails; fix with try_files fallback to index.html, or set VITE_ROUTER_HISTORY_MODE=hash when the web server cannot be changed.

nodes.label: Git Hooks Pre-commit Checks (simple-git-hooks)
nodes.rationale: Pre-commit checks raise code quality and cut maintenance cost; SoybeanAdmin has 100% TypeScript type coverage. Can be bypassed temporarily with --no-verify or removed permanently by deleting simple-git-hooks commands (not recommended).

nodes.label: Local SVG Icon Rendering (vite-plugin-svg-icons, src/assets/svg-icon)
nodes.rationale: SVG files become static Vue components at build time, so changes to source SVG files require a project restart.

nodes.label: main vs example Branch Strategy
nodes.rationale: main branch carries only the core framework for easy adoption; example branch contains the full sample menus shown in the preview site.

nodes.label: Expired Token Refresh Flow (handleRefreshToken + retry)
nodes.rationale: When the backend code is in VITE_SERVICE_EXPIRED_TOKEN_CODES and no refresh is in flight, the instance refreshes the token and retries the original request; the refreshToken endpoint must never return expired-token codes to avoid infinite loops.

nodes.label: Route Guard
nodes.rationale: Central navigation control flow of SoybeanAdmin; documented only via a flowchart image and high-resolution PDF rather than prose.

nodes.label: Single Root Element Constraint (Transition)
nodes.rationale: Because page transition animations use Vue's <Transition>, every view .vue template must have exactly one root element (no comments or bare text at root).

nodes.label: type LoginModule
nodes.rationale: Union of login page modules: pwd-login | code-login | register | reset-pwd | bind-wechat.

nodes.label: Multi-level Route (underscore flattening)
nodes.rationale: For routes deeper than 2 levels, a flat 2-layer folder structure using underscores (e.g. multi-menu/first_child) is recommended to avoid deep folder nesting; generated route data becomes recursive but converted Vue routes stay 2 layers.

nodes.label: Ignored Folder Aggregated Routes (_ prefix)
nodes.rationale: Folder names starting with underscore (e.g. _error) are ignored in route paths; their children (403/404/500) are hoisted to the parent level.

nodes.label: Code Sync via cherry-pick
nodes.rationale: Downstream projects keep up with upstream soybean-admin by adding it as a second git remote (otherOrigin), fetching, and cherry-picking selected commits, resolving conflicts with cherry-pick --continue.

nodes.label: getNaiveTheme
nodes.rationale: Generates NaiveUI GlobalThemeOverrides from App.Theme.ThemeColor; applied via NConfigProvider in src/App.vue.

nodes.label: getAntdTheme
nodes.rationale: Generates AntDesignVue theme tokens and algorithm (dark/default) from App.Theme.ThemeColor and darkMode; applied via ConfigProvider.

nodes.label: themeVars (UnoCSS theme injection)
nodes.rationale: Injecting theme tokens from src/theme/vars into UnoCSS theme config enables classes like text-primary / bg-primary so UnoCSS and component-library theme colors stay unified.

nodes.label: UnoCSS Dark Mode (class-based) (2)
nodes.rationale: Uses presetUno({ dark: 'class' }); adding class="dark" on html enables dark: variant utilities.

nodes.label: SoybeanAdmin (3)
nodes.rationale: Elegant admin template based on Vue3, Vite6, TypeScript, UnoCSS; pnpm monorepo; supports Vue3/React and multiple UI libraries; file-based routing; static frontend and dynamic backend permission routing.

nodes.label: SoybeanUI (@soybeanjs/ui)
nodes.rationale: Promoted Vue 3 component system (91+ components) combining headless interaction with ready-to-use styled implementations.

nodes.label: Recommended Technologies (intro)
nodes.rationale: Section presenting interesting technologies not necessarily adopted by the project but considered valuable references.

nodes.label: Alova (3)
nodes.rationale: Next-generation request tool with axios-like API, client/server (SSR) support, multi-level caching and request sharing; collapses API integration workflow from 7 steps to 1.

nodes.label: klona (2)
nodes.rationale: Tiny (240B-501B gzip) deep-clone utility with tiered builds (json/lite/default/full) supporting Date, RegExp, Map, Set, TypedArray, Symbol properties.

nodes.label: PageSpy

nodes.label: empty-data.svg — empty-state illustration
nodes.rationale: 500x500 flat vector empty-state scene: pale gray elliptical ground; on the left a stack of five isometric dark blue-gray (#263238/#455a64/#37474f) storage crates/server boxes with rows of small LED-like indicator dots and theme-colored accent stripes; center shows a large tilted white document board whose 'NO D...' letterforms (N/O/D glyphs) are drawn as vector paths, signalling 'no data'; upper right a theme-colored magnifying glass (loupe) with handle, implying a fruitless search; flat platform cards sit at lower right. All accent elements use fill="currentColor" so the highlight color inherits the surrounding text/theme color.

nodes.label: currentColor theme-adaptive accent technique
nodes.rationale: Dozens of paths in the illustration are filled with currentColor instead of a hard-coded hex value, while structural parts keep fixed grays. This lets the same SVG asset recolor its accent stripes, loupe, and highlight planes to whatever theme/primary color the host component applies via CSS `color`, avoiding per-theme asset duplication — the standard convention for soybean-admin local svg-icon illustrations.

nodes.label: Empty-state UI illustration pattern

Accent areas (clothing etc.) use fill:currentColor in 22 places so the artwork inherits the active theme's primary color from its container instead of needing per-theme asset variants; remaining fills are fixed grayscale (#ebebeb/#e0e0e0) and skin/outline tones (#ffbe9d/#263238). nodes.label: network-error.svg (network error illustration)
nodes.description: Flat-style 500x500 vector illustration depicting a network/connectivity error state: a person stands next to an oversized smartphone whose screen shows a WiFi symbol overlaid by a large circle-with-diagonal-slash (no-connection sign). The phone has a realistic status bar (clock digits, signal-strength bars, small WiFi icon with dot, battery outline). Scene props include a wilted potted plant, a chair with striped cushion, a window-grid pane, and a ground line. Dark strokes/fills use #263238; accent areas (background blob, slashed circle, person's clothing, cushion) use fill=currentColor so the illustration adapts to the app theme color. nodes.label: currentColor theme adaptation in network-error.svg
nodes.rationale: The illustration's accent shapes (background blob, no-connection slash circle, clothing, cushion) are filled with currentColor instead of hard-coded hues, so when rendered through the app's SvgIcon/local-icon pipeline the graphic automatically inherits the active theme color, keeping error/empty-state pages visually consistent with any user-selected theme without shipping per-theme image variants.

nodes.label: defaultLocalIcon missing-icon fallback
nodes.rationale: The SvgIcon component hardcodes defaultLocalIcon = 'no-icon' so that when neither the iconify icon prop nor the localIcon prop resolves, it renders the local no-icon.svg asset. The asset is deliberately drawn as a broken heart (Fluent-emoji style: two pink/magenta gradient heart halves separated by a jagged crack), making a missing or misnamed icon visibly obvious in the UI instead of rendering nothing.

nodes.label: No-Permission (403) Illustration
nodes.rationale: 500x500 flat-vector scene: large isometric '403' digits next to an open door blocked by diagonal caution/barrier tape, a warning signboard with an exclamation mark and fine-print text, and a cartoon person standing to the right. Greys (#37474f/#455a64/#e0e0e0) carry the structure while accent shapes use fill=currentColor, signalling 'access forbidden' on the error page.

nodes.label: currentColor Theme-Adaptive SVG Coloring
nodes.rationale: The illustration's accent paths use fill="currentColor" instead of hard-coded hues so the artwork automatically inherits the active theme/primary color of the admin UI; only neutral greys and skin tones are fixed. This lets one asset match any theme without per-theme variants.

nodes.label: not-found.svg (404 Page Not Found Illustration)

Accent shapes use fill="currentColor" so the artwork tints to the active theme's primary color at render time (ExceptionBase wraps the icon in a text-primary container), making the error art theme-adaptive without per-theme image assets.

nodes.label: ExceptionBase component
nodes.rationale: Single shared exception page component: an iconMap maps exception type '403'->'no-permission', '404'->'not-found', '500'->'service-error', and renders the selected local SVG icon at text-400px inside a text-primary wrapper plus a back-to-home button.
